fullPassage:
Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to announce a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!

Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.

Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.

Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.

Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.

It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.

Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.

Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: announcing → announce (expect to 뒤 to부정사이므로 동사원형)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: narrowest → narrower (「the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 ~」 구문이라 비교급 narrower, 최상급 불가)
det.analysis:
① noticed: 'you probably noticed that' 과거동사 — 적절해요.

② hit: 'strong winds ... hit a tall building' 복수 주어에 맞는 동사원형 hit — 적절해요.

③ narrowest: 'the narrowest the space, the faster it moves'? '~하면 할수록 더 …하다'라는 「the+비교급, the+비교급」 구문이에요. 이 구문에는 최상급(narrowest)이 아니라 비교급 narrower를 써야 하므로 틀려요 ←정답

③ behavioral: 행동 치료로 다룸 — 적절

④ growing: 동시동작을 나타내는 분사 growing — 적절

det.korean: absorb → absorbs (관계대명사 which의 선행사 the dark water가 단수이므로 단수동사 absorbs)

② 최소한으로만 유지하려 한다: 'own as many things as possible(가능한 한 많이 소유)'과 반대예요.

③ 원인이 하나로 명확해 치료가 빠르다: 'a complex condition with multiple causes ~ takes a long time(원인이 여럿이라 오래 걸림)'과 반대예요.

④ 쓸모없는 물건을 버리지 못하는 무능력과 관련된 정신 질환: 첫 문장 정의(the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value)와 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: 핵심 정의: inability to get rid of useless possessions = 쓸모없는 물건을 못 버림

ch: 저장 강박은 나이가 들수록 저절로 나아진다.
저장 강박은 원인이 하나로 명확해 치료가 빠르다.
저장 강박은 쓸모없는 물건을 버리지 못하는 무능력과 관련된 정신 질환이다.

questions.passage: Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does <u>this practice</u> benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 this practice가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: this practice = 단체들이 못난이 농산물을 사서 소비자에게 (더 싸게) 파는 관행
det.analysis:
밑줄 친 'this practice(이 관행)'는 바로 앞 문장에서 설명한 활동을 가리켜요. 앞 문장은 '단체들이 농부에게서 못난이 농산물을 사서 소비자에게 정상가보다 싸게 판다'는 내용이에요.

① 수확물을 겉모습 때문에 버리는 일: 이것은 관행이 해결하려는 '문제'이지 this practice가 아님 — 오답

② 단체들이 못난이 농산물을 사서 소비자에게 파는 일: 바로 앞 문장에서 소개한 활동으로, 농부·소비자·환경 모두에 이롭다고 이어짐 ←정답

③ 슈퍼마켓이 똑같이 생긴 농산물을 진열하는 일: this practice가 가리키는 활동이 아님 — 오답

④ 농부들이 원치 않는 농산물을 재배하는 일: 오히려 그럴 필요가 없어진다고 했으므로 반대 — 오답
det.tip: 바로 앞 문장 = 못난이 농산물을 사서 소비자에게 파는 일 → this practice

ch: 수확물의 절반가량을 겉모습 때문에 버리는 일
단체들이 못난이 농산물을 사서 소비자에게 파는 일
슈퍼마켓이 똑같이 생긴 농산물을 진열하는 일

questions.passage: Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that ①<u>uses</u> the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it ②<u>compares</u> the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need ③<u>carrying</u> credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to ④<u>fool</u> than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ carrying → to carry: need(필요하다)는 목적어로 to부정사를 취하므로 need to carry
det.analysis:
✅ ① uses — 'biometrics that ① uses the palm(손바닥을 사용하는 생체 인식)'에서 선행사가 단수라 관계사절 동사도 단수 uses, 적절해요.

✅ ② compares — 'it ② compares the patterns(그것이 패턴을 비교한다)'는 주어 it에 맞춘 단수 동사, 적절해요.

❌ ③ carrying — 'people no longer need ③ carrying credit cards(사람들은 신용카드를 가지고 다닐 필요가 없다)'에서 need는 목적어로 동명사(-ing)가 아니라 to부정사를 취해요. 그래서 carrying이 아니라 to carry로 써서 'need to carry'가 되어야 해요 → 틀려요 ←정답

✅ ④ fool — 'harder to ④ fool(속이기 더 어려운)'은 형용사 harder를 꾸미는 to부정사, 적절해요.
det.tip: need + to부정사. need carrying(X) → need to carry(O)

questions.passage: It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문 'solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects'의 패러프레이즈 → 일치
det.analysis:
① 사하라는 세계에서 '가장 큰(largest)' 사막이라고 했으므로 '두 번째'는 틀려요.

② 사막의 대규모 태양광 발전이 부정적 환경 영향을 낳을 수 있다는 내용을 바꿔 말한 것으로 일치해요 ←정답

③ 온난화는 사막에 국한되지 않고 지구 전체로 퍼진다고 했어요.

④ 어두운 물은 해빙보다 에너지를 '더 많이' 흡수한다고 했으므로 '덜 흡수'는 반대예요.
det.tip: adverse environmental effects(부정적 영향)를 패러프레이즈한 ②가 유일하게 일치

ch: 사하라는 세계에서 두 번째로 큰 사막이다.
사막의 대규모 태양광 발전은 부정적인 환경 영향을 낳을 수 있다.
어두운 바닷물은 해빙보다 태양 에너지를 덜 흡수한다.

questions.passage: Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문 S1 'apply it to men rather than women'을 바꿔 말함 → 일치
det.analysis:
① 여성보다 남성에게 더 자주 부여함 = 'we usually apply it to men rather than women'을 바꿔 말함 ←정답(일치)
② 겨우 수천 건? 본문은 '1,400만 건(14 million)'을 분석함 — 불일치
③ 여성 비율이 높음? 본문은 물리·철학이 여성이 '적은(few)' 분야라고 함 — 불일치
④ 최근 특정 국가에서? 본문은 '전 세계적으로(all across the world)' 일어난다고 함 — 불일치
det.tip: apply it to men rather than women = 남성에게 더 자주 부여(일치)

ch: 사람들은 '뛰어난(brilliant)'이라는 칭찬을 여성보다 남성에게 더 자주 부여하는 경향이 있다.
2016년 연구는 겨우 수천 건의 강의 후기만을 분석 대상으로 삼았다.
물리학과 철학은 여성 비율이 유난히 높은 분야로 나타났다.
이러한 편견은 최근에야 특정 국가에서 처음 생겨난 현상이다.

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 'had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent' → 두 배 차이 → 불일치
det.analysis:
① 따뜻한 물이 백화·죽음: 'threatened by unusually warm water ... to bleach and die'와 일치

② 안전한 서식지 신호: 'it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live'와 일치

③ 조용해 서식 동물 거의 못 끌어들여 악화: 'Damaged reefs ... are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further'와 일치

④ 물고기 수 차이 없음? ←정답(불일치): 소리를 튼 곳은 조용히 둔 곳보다 '두 배 많은(twice as many)' 어린 물고기를 끌어들였어요. 차이가 없었다는 것은 반대예요.
det.tip: 소리 튼 곳 = 조용한 곳의 twice as many(두 배). '차이 없음'은 반대

ch: 이례적으로 따뜻한 물이 산호초의 백화와 죽음을 일으킨다.
건강한 산호초의 소리는 어린 물고기에게 안전한 서식지 신호가 된다.
손상된 산호초는 조용해 새로운 서식 동물을 거의 못 끌어들이고 더 나빠진다.
실험에서 소리를 튼 곳과 조용히 둔 곳의 어린 물고기 수는 차이가 없었다.

questions.passage: Local elementary schools are ①<u>forced</u> to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The ②<u>theme</u> of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot ③<u>featuring</u> the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to ④<u>announce</u> a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① forced=강요받은 → invited(초대받은) ② theme=주제 ③ featuring=특별히 포함하는 ④ announce=발표하다
det.analysis:
① forced: 'join us(우리와 함께하자)'는 함께하도록 '초대'(invited)하는 다정한 권유예요. '강요받은'(forced)은 정반대라 부적절해요. ←정답

② theme: 포스터의 '주제'는 공동체 통합 — 적절

③ featuring: 우승자를 '특별히 포함'한 사진 촬영 — 적절

④ announce: 우승자를 '발표'하려는 흐름 — 적절
det.tip: join us(함께하자)에 어울리는 건 invited(초대). forced(강요)는 정반대

questions.passage: Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or __________. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: straight into the windows=곧장 창문 안으로 / around the sides of the building=건물의 옆면을 돌아서 / back up into the clouds=구름 속으로 되돌아 / deep under the street=거리 깊은 아래로
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or ___(그것을 통과할 수 없어서, 대신 위로, 아래로, 혹은 ___ 간다)'예요. 건물을 통과하지 못한 바람이 갈 수 있는 방향을 생각해요.

① straight into the windows(곧장 창문 안으로): 통과 못 한다고 했으니 안으로 들어가는 건 반대

② around the sides of the building(건물 옆면을 돌아서): 위·아래와 나란히 '건물 옆면을 돌아서' 간다는 흐름과 일치 ←정답

③ back up into the clouds(구름 속으로): 본문에 없는 내용

④ deep under the street(거리 깊은 아래로): 땅속으로 간다는 내용은 없음
det.tip: 통과 못 함 → 위·아래·옆(around the sides)으로 감

ch: around the sides of the building

questions.passage: Hoarding disorder is a mental ①<u>illness</u> characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive ②<u>acquisition</u>," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior ③<u>tends</u> to start at an early age and becomes more and more ④<u>mild</u> as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① illness=질환 ② acquisition=습득 ③ tends=경향이 있다 ④ extreme→mild (부적절)
det.analysis:
① illness: 저장 강박은 정신 질환 — 적절

② acquisition: 과도한 '습득'을 동반함 — 적절

③ tends: 이른 나이에 시작되는 '경향이 있음' — 적절

④ mild: 나이가 들수록 점점 '더 온화(mild)'해진다? 뒤이어 '점점 더(more and more)'라는 심화의 표현이 오고 치료가 필요해지는 흐름이라, 점점 '더 극심(extreme)'해진다가 원문이에요. mild(온화한)는 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: more and more ~ = 점점 더 심해짐. extreme(극심한)이 맞고 mild(온화한)는 반대

questions.passage: Have you ever seen rows of ①<u>identical</u> fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their ②<u>harvest</u> because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ③<u>attractive</u> produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste ④<u>resources</u> growing unwanted produce.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ attractive → ugly. 단체들이 사들이는 것은 '못난이(ugly)' 농산물
det.analysis:

④ resources: 원치 않는 농산물을 기르느라 낭비되는 '자원(resources)' — 적절
